claim: Gemini Embedding 2 is the strongest all-rounder for multilingual and cross-modal retrieval; MTEB leaderboard misses cross-modal, long-document accuracy, and dimension compression.
quote: No single model wins everything. Gemini Embedding 2 is the strongest overall for cross-lingual tasks, achieving perfect 1.000 on the Hard tier with Chinese idioms.

claim: Open-weight models match or exceed closed APIs on MTEB v2; self-hosting crossover is ~500M–1B tokens/month; BGE-M3 costs ~$500/month vs ~$13,000/month for OpenAI at comparable scale.
quote: Self-hosted BGE-M3 yields approximately $500 per month versus $13,000 per month for OpenAI's service at comparable scale.

claim: The retrieval quality curve flattens past 768 dims; MRL-trained models retain 93–95% retrieval quality when truncated from 1536 to 256 dims at 6x lower storage.
quote: A 1536-dimensional embedding reduced to 256 dimensions retains approximately 93–95% of the retrieval quality while reducing storage sixfold.

claim: Chunking quality constrains retrieval accuracy more than embedding model choice; best-vs-worst gap is ~9% recall; recursive 512-token scored 69% vs semantic 54% in benchmarks.
quote: The wrong chunking approach can open a gap of up to 9% in recall between the best and worst methods on the same corpus, with the same retriever.

claim: Late chunking improves nDCG@10 by 1.8–1.9% over naive chunking on BEIR datasets; gains grow with document length.
quote: Fixed-size boundaries: 3.46% relative improvement (1.8% absolute) in nDCG@10. Sentence boundaries: 3.63% relative improvement (1.9% absolute).

claim: Late chunking embeds all document tokens first, then splits the token-embedding sequence before mean pooling, preserving contextual references.
quote: First, encode all tokens of an entire document with their full in-document context into a sequence of token embeddings, and then break this sequence up into chunks.

claim: HNSW delivers ~98%+ recall and sub-ms latency but degrades severely when filter ratios exceed 90%; IVF uses lower memory and maintains stable performance with filtered search.
quote: When filtering ratios exceed 90%, the graph becomes fragmented and may degrade to near full-graph traversal, even slower than brute-force search.

claim: Under 10M vectors any store works; 10M–1B narrows to Qdrant/Weaviate/Milvus/Pinecone; Qdrant p50 latency ~4ms, Milvus ~6ms; Chroma degrades above hundreds of thousands of vectors.
quote: Qdrant delivers the lowest p50 latency of any purpose-built vector database — roughly 4ms, compared to Milvus at ~6ms and Pinecone at ~8ms.

claim: The production retrieval pattern is BM25+dense → RRF fusion → cross-encoder rerank; RRF sidesteps score-incompatibility by working on rank position.
quote: Hybrid retrieval fuses both via Reciprocal Rank Fusion — a rank-only algorithm that sidesteps the score-incompatibility problem that breaks naively-weighted pipelines.

claim: In naive embedding pipelines, GPU inference accounts for only ~10% of compute; disaggregated tokenization + multiple model replicas achieved 16x throughput improvement at 230k tokens/sec on A10g.
quote: The embedding function accounts for just 10% of total compute time. The remaining 90% is spent on CPU tasks. 16x and 4.2x higher embedding throughput for short (50 tokens) and long sequences (512 tokens), respectively.

claim: Binary quantization achieves 32x compression and 80% faster queries but requires a rescoring pass to recover precision.
quote: Binary quantization converts floats into binary bits, resulting in up to 28 times reduced vector index size. Binary quantization yields a 32x compression factor but the substantial precision loss often requires a subsequent rescoring step.

claim: Combined INT8 quantization and dimensionality reduction cuts embedding storage 4–8x with under 1% MTEB score drop.
quote: Optimization of embeddings storage for RAG systems using quantization and dimensionality reduction techniques.

claim: INT8 quantization drops MTEB scores by less than 0.5% while CPUs can process 8-bit integers significantly faster than floating-point numbers.
quote: CPUs can process 8-bit integers significantly faster than floating-point numbers, with MTEB scores dropping by less than 0.5% after INT8 quantization.

claim: Sentence chunking matches semantic chunking performance for documents under ~5,000 tokens.
quote: Sentence chunking equivalence: Matches semantic performance up to ~5,000 tokens.

claim: Contextual Retrieval alone reduces top-20 retrieval failures by 35%; combined with reranking, the reduction reaches 67%, with preprocessing cost ~$1.02/M tokens.
quote: Contextual Embeddings alone reduced top-20 retrieval failures by about 35%, and combined with reranking the reduction reached roughly 67%, with a one-time preprocessing cost of about $1.02 per million document tokens using prompt caching.

claim: Switching embedding models forces a full re-index; on consumer hardware, every embedder swap costs 30–90 minutes per 5,000 pages.
quote: Switching embedders forces a full re-index, and no local RAG platform supports incremental migration, with every embedder swap costing 30–90 minutes per 5,000 pages on consumer hardware.

claim: Top vector databases in 2026 include Chroma, Pinecone, Weaviate, FAISS, Qdrant, Milvus, and pgvector; RAG is the primary adoption driver.
quote: The top vector databases in 2026 include Chroma, Pinecone, Weaviate, Faiss, Qdrant, Milvus, and pgvector. Key selection factors include scale requirements, managed vs. self-hosted preference, existing tech stack, and budget.

claim: IVF-PQ reduces memory 4–8x while maintaining 95%+ recall rates; a billion-vector dataset requires only ~500 GB vs 4 TB for HNSW.
quote: IVF-PQ reduces memory usage by 4-8x while maintaining 95%+ recall rates, with a billion-vector dataset requiring only 500GB compared to 4TB with HNSW.

claim: Hybrid BM25+dense+cross-encoder reranking delivered +48% RAG accuracy in production; BM25 handles exact-match queries that break dense retrieval.
quote: One team achieved 48% better RAG accuracy using cascading retrieval with BM25, FAISS, and cross-encoder reranking in production.

claim: A January 2026 systematic analysis found chunk overlap adds no measurable retrieval benefit and increases indexing cost.
quote: Overlap provides no measurable benefit and increases indexing cost. Universal 10–20% overlap recommendations are now contested; treat as tunable rather than mandatory default.

claim: Self-hosting via Hugging Face Text Embeddings Inference (TEI) on GPU cloud is straightforward for teams crossing the ~500M token/month threshold.
quote: Self-Host Embeddings and Rerankers: TEI on GPU Cloud (2026).

claim: The retrieve top-1000 → cross-encoder rerank top-100 pattern stays within p99 latency budgets for interactive search; cross-encoders jointly encode query+document for precise scoring.
quote: The pattern retrieve top-1000 → rerank top-100 is well within p99 latency budgets for interactive search. Cross-encoders process query + document together through a transformer, which allows attention mechanisms to model their interaction directly.
